 Search Advertisement Basketball Home › Sports › Basketball Why These 4 Teams in the PBA Governors’ Cup Are Worth Rooting For
 By  Sid Ventura - October 29, 2026 The format of the ongoing PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup has ensured that one of the teams in the finals won’t be from the usual suspects , and that’s a good thing. 
 The season-ending PBA Governors’ Cup is now in playoff mode. Only eight teams remain in the crossover Crossover A basketball dribbling move in which a player quickly switches the ball from one hand to the other to change direction and beat a defender. A good crossover creates space Go to Crossover Glossary quarterfinals, and looking at the playoff brackets, one thing is certain: a team from among the NLEX Road Warriors, Converge FiberXers, Phoenix Fuel Masters and Rain or Shine Elasto Painters will make it to the finals.
 This is a significant development because ever since the 2019 Philippine Cup, 15 of the 16 championship series have featured a combination of finalists limited to the San Miguel Beermen, Barangay Ginebra San Miguel, Magnolia Hotshots, TNT Tropang 5G, and Meralco Bolts. The only other team to break that stranglehold were the guest team Bay Area Dragons.
 Now, thanks to a quirk in the playoff bracketing, another team will get to sneak in.
 How did this happen? You can thank the league for implementing a two-group format for the elimination round, where teams played other teams in their group twice, with the top four moving on to the crossover Crossover A basketball dribbling move in which a player quickly switches the ball from one hand to the other to change direction and beat a defender. A good crossover creates space Go to Crossover Glossary quarterfinals.
 As it turned out, NLEX topped Group A, followed by SMB, Converge and TNT. Over in Group B, Magnolia grabbed the no. 1 seed, followed by Rain or Shine, Barangay Ginebra and Phoenix.
 This resulted in a Governors’ Cup playoff bracket putting NLEX, Phoenix, Rain or Shine and Converge on one side, and usual finalists SMB, Ginebra, TNT and Magnolia on the other in a virtual Group of Death.
 It would certainly be refreshing to see a new team in the finals, which is what would happen if NLEX or Converge or Phoenix makes it through. But it would also be nice to see Yeng Guiao and his Elasto Painters back in the Big Dance, especially since they were the last “independent” team to win a title, which they did 10 years ago.
 But what level of excitement or drama can each of these “unconventional” teams offer to viewers? Let’s break it down.
 NLEX Road Warriors – Return of the Prodigal Son
 The biggest storyline going for the Road Warriors in the Governors’ Cup is their coach. Jimmy Alapag turned down offers from a number of NBA teams to come home and coach NLEX, and so far he’s done a very good job. The Road Warriors finished with a 9-3 record, which included two wins over TNT and one over SMB. If they make it all the way and eventually lift the trophy, it would be the perfect homecoming for Alapag and vindicate his decision to shun NBA offers.
 There’s also a brewing side story for Robert Bolick, who currently leads the statistical race for Best Player of the Conference and who has never played in a PBA finals. If Berto can lead his team to the promised land, then it will certainly boost his MVP chances while elevating his status among the league’s best guards.
 Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters – How Did We Get Here?
 It’s tempting to look at the Fuel Masters’ team statistics and dismiss them right away. How can a team whose import isn’t even in the top 10 of the Best Import statistical race, who doesn’t have a single local player in the top 20 of the BPC, and who’s missing its best local player be in the quarterfinals Quarterfinals The round of a tournament in which eight remaining competitors play to determine the four who advance to the semifinals. Quarterfinals mark the exciting point where contenders emerge, and in Go to Quarterfinals Glossary ?
 Yet that’s exactly why they have a compelling story. Somehow, even after replacing the prolific Robert Johnson III with a relatively ordinary Marcellus Earlington, and even after losing Jason Perkins to a serious foot injury, here they are in the playoffs, pushing the Road Warriors in their first two quarterfinal games.
 The brightest spark in Phoenix’s story is the emergence of Ricci Rivero, who has become their primary option on offense with Perkins sidelined. The Fuel Masters may be down 0-2 as of posting time, but there’s still a lot of fight in them.
 Converge FiberXers – Come Juan, Come All
 If you’re the type of fan who shies away from traditional powerhouses and prefers to root for a wildcard that’s fun to watch, then the FiberXers are the team for you.
 Led by the immensely talented Juan Gomez de Liaño, who is a virtual lock for Rookie of the Year, the FiberXers have found a new groove under Serbian consultant Djordje Jovivic. Prior to their game 1 loss to Rain or Shine, they had won six in a row and looked like they were having fun doing it.
 Their Justin-Justine low post combo Combo In fighting games, a sequence of attacks that connect so the opponent cannot block or escape between hits. Mastering combos requires practice, timing, and knowledge of character mechanics, and the Go to Combo Glossary of Arana and Baltazar are running second and third in the BPC race, proof of their overall firepower. Then there’s the veteran provocateur Calvin Abueva and the pesky Alec Stockton, who make sure there’s never a dull moment on the court. If Converge advance deep into the playoffs, they’ll be a hot ticket.
 Rain or Shine Elasto Painters – One More Chance for Yeng
 The Elasto Painters have been knocking on the door of a finals for a few seasons now. They always came up short in the semifinals, where they would run into one of the powerhouses like TNT or Ginebra. But thanks to this particular bracket Bracket The tournament chart that organizes matches and shows how winners advance toward the final, in formats such as single elimination or double elimination. Brackets allow fans to follow a team's Go to Bracket Glossary , they have a legitimate chance of finally advancing to the finals.
 If so, it would be a nice comeback of sorts for coach Yeng Guiao and his merry men. Rain or Shine, led by their fiery coach, has long represented the common man, the no-frills team that dares rage against the corporate machinery of the two major conglomerates.
 They don’t have a flashy import, and their heart and soul in Gabe Norwood is no longer around, but Guiao has once again worked his magic and turned players like Adrian Nocum, Jhonard Clarito and Vince Cuajao into legitimate PBA stars. You cant help but root for them.

 Frequently Asked Questions
 How did a non-traditional finalist become guaranteed in the Governors’ Cup?
 A two-group elimination format created a bracket where NLEX, Phoenix, Rain or Shine, and Converge all landed on one side, guaranteeing a non-traditional finalist.
 What’s the biggest storyline behind NLEX’s playoff run?
 Coach Jimmy Alapag turned down NBA offers to lead NLEX to a 9-3 record, while Robert Bolick’s strong BPC campaign adds another compelling storyline.
 How has Phoenix reached the quarterfinals despite its lineup struggles?
 Phoenix reached the quarterfinals despite losing Jason Perkins to injury and replacing Robert Johnson III, with Ricci Rivero emerging as their primary scoring option.
 What has fueled Converge’s strong playoff push?
 Converge, led by Rookie of the Year favorite Juan Gomez de Liaño, won six straight games under Serbian consultant Djordje Jovivic before their quarterfinal opener.
 Why is this a big opportunity for Rain or Shine and Yeng Guiao?
 Rain or Shine, led by coach Yeng Guiao, has fallen short in past semifinals but has a legitimate shot at the finals through this bracket.
